why: Intercept form x/a + y/b = 1 at (1,1) gives 1/a + 1/b = 1.
E = midpoint AC = (3/2, -7/2); line through B(-2,3) has slope -13/7, i.e. 13x + 7y + 5 = 0 (only option vanishing at both B and E).
Equal intercepts gives x + y = a; through (1,2) gives a = 3. (The degenerate zero-intercept line y = 2x also fits the wording but appears in no option.)
The two lines meet at (-1,2); kx + 4y = 6 then gives -k + 8 = 6, so k = 2.

Slope tan 120 = -sqrt3 gives sqrt3 x + y = c with |c|/2 = 3, so sqrt3 x + y +- 6 = 0; option A varies the sign of y instead, whose minus branch has slope +sqrt3 (inclination 60), so only one of its two branches is valid.
Perpendicular slope 1/3 through (2,2) gives x - 3y + 4 = 0, so the y-intercept is 4/3.
Slopes sqrt3 and 1/sqrt3 give inclinations 60 and 30, so the angle is 30.
Dividing 6x - 4y + 2 = 0 by -2 gives -3x + 2y - 1 = 0, matching kx + 2y - 1 = 0 with k = -3.
